body_text: Stantec delivers strong second quarter 2026 results, expands margins and raises adjusted EBITDA outlook for 2026 08/12/2026 PDF Version Net revenue of $1.8 billion, an increase of 11.5% compared to Q2 2025 Adjusted EBITDA1 increase of 17.1% to $332.9 million and adjusted EBITDA margin1 of 18.7%, a 90 basis point increase over Q2 2025 Diluted EPS of $1.32 and adjusted EPS1 of $1.61, up 10.9% and 18.4%, respectively, compared to Q2 2025 Contract backlog increased to $9.2 billion, up 17.5% year-over-year Repurchased 1,667,292 common shares for an aggregate price of $175.9 million in the first two quarters of 2026 On July 31, 2026 Stantec acquired Niche, a 200-person engineering and environmental consultancy firm in Australia, bolstering its Environmental Services operations. EDMONTON, Alberta and NEW YORK, Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Stantec (TSX, NYSE:STN), a global leader in sustainable engineering, architecture and environmental consulting, released its second quarter 2026 results today. In the second quarter, net revenue increased 11.5% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, driven by acquisition growth1 of 7.1%, primarily reflecting strong results from Page in our US operations, and organic growth of 3.7% which was driven primarily by 12.8% organic growth in Global. Second quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA increased 17.1% or $48.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin reached 18.7%, up 90 basis points compared to the second quarter 2025. Stantec delivered diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.32 and adjusted EPS of $1.61. On a year-to-date basis, net revenue increased 10.3% to $3.5 billion, driven by 7.2% acquisition and 3.7% organic growth. All of Stantec's operating regions have achieved organic net revenue growth year-to-date, with Water achieving 13.0% organic net revenue growth. Adjusted EBITDA increased 15.5% to $619.9 million year-to-date, and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 80 basis points over the prior period to 17.8%. Adjusted EPS increased 16.7% to $2.94. “As reflected in Stantec's second quarter results, strong operational performance, combined with solid growth in our Global region and meaningful contributions from our acquisition of Page, have kept us on track to deliver on our 2026 financial targets,” said Gord Johnston, President and CEO. “The long-term demand drivers of our business remain intact, and with a record backlog of $9.2 billion, we expect to see an acceleration of activity in the second half of 2026.” __________________________ 1 Adjusted EPS, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow to net income are non-IFRS measures; organic growth and acquisition growth are other financial measures (discussed in the Definitions section of Stantec's Q2 2026 Management's Discussion and Analysis). 2026 Outlook Stantec is reaffirming its 2026 guidance while narrowing and adjusting upward its adjusted EBITDA target for the year. 2026 Annual Range Targets Net revenue growth 8.5% to 11.5% Adjusted EBITDA as % of net revenue (note) 17.8% to 18.3% Adjusted net income as % of net revenue (note) at or above 9.5% Adjusted EPS growth (note) 15% to 18% Adjusted ROIC (note) above 13% In setting targets and guidance, Stantec assumed an average value for the US dollar of $1.38, GBP of $1.85, and AU of $0.98 for the remainder of the year. For all other underlying assumptions, see page M-20. note: Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income, adjusted EPS, and adjusted ROIC are non-IFRS measures discussed in the Definitions section of Stantec's Q2 2026 Management's Discussion and Analysis. The global environment is dynamic, and customer needs continue to evolve, as do public sector policy and investment priorities. While year-to-date results position Stantec favorably to achieve its initial estimate of net revenue growth of 8.5% to 11.5% in 2026, the Company has refined its outlook and now expects organic net revenue growth to be in the mid-single digit range. In the United States, the organic growth in backlog and other customer demand signals support Stantec's continued expectation that results will improve across our business lines and yield mid-single digit organic net revenue growth for the year. In Canada, Stantec also expects organic net revenue growth to improve moderately and achieve mid-single digits by year end, supported by public sector spending plans and continued demand, particularly in our Water and Buildings business lines. Lastly, Stantec continues to expect Global to maintain strong organic net revenue growth in the high-single digits, supported by continued high levels of activity in its Water business under the ongoing Asset Management Program and frameworks, strong demand in Energy & Resources, and positive demand fundamentals across other Global business units. Stantec's year-to-date results reflect strong margin improvements and effectiveness in managing operating costs, and the Company has refined its estimate of adjusted EBITDA margin accordingly. Stantec expects that adjusted EBITDA margin will reach a record range of 17.8% to 18.3% in 2026, reflecting an increase in the low end of its targeted range from 17.6% to 17.8%, and an increase in the high end of the range from 18.2% to 18.3%. This improvement reflects strong project margins resulting from solid project execution, as well as continued focus on enhanced strategies in the management of administration and marketing costs. These initiatives include the continued expansion of Stantec's high-value centers, optimization of digital strategies, and increased efficiencies from improved scale in certain key geographies. Overall, Stantec expects to achieve an adjusted net income margin at or above 9.5% of net revenue, an adjusted ROIC greater than 13%, and to deliver 15% to 18% growth in adjusted EPS compared to 2025. The above targets do not include any assumptions related to additional acquisitions, given the unpredictable nature of the timing and size of such transactions. Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025 Stantec achieved strong second quarter adjusted net income of $182.5 million and adjusted earnings per share of $1.61, reflecting an increase of 18.4%, driven by net revenue growth and strong operational performance. Net revenue increased 11.5% or $183.9 million, to $1.8 billion, driven by acquisition growth of 7.1%, which primarily reflects the strong results of Page in Stantec's US operations, and organic growth of 3.7%. Organic growth was driven by Stantec's Global region of 12.8%. Project margin increased 12.3% or $106.0 million, to $970.7 million as a result of net revenue growth and solid project execution. Project margin, as a percentage of net revenue, increased by 30 basis points to 54.5%. Adjusted EBITDA increased 17.1% or $48.5 million, to $332.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.7%, an increase of 90 basis points compared to Q2 2025. The growth in margin was primarily due to the increase in net revenue, solid project margin, and lower administrative and marketing expenses as a percentage of net revenue, reflecting our focus on efficient management of operations and optimization of discretionary spending. Net income increased 11.0% or $14.9 million, to $150.3 million, and diluted EPS increased 11.0%, or $0.13, to $1.32, mainly due to net revenue growth and solid project margin, and, as a percentage of net revenue, a 110 basis point reduction in administrative and marketing expenses, partly offset by impairment recorded on lease assets and higher amortization of intangible assets as a result of Stantec's recent acquisitions. Adjusted net income grew 18.0% or $27.8 million, to $182.5 million, achieving 10.2% of net revenue—an increase of 50 basis points compared to Q2 2025. Adjusted EPS increased 18.4% or $0.25, to $1.61. Contract backlog grew to $9.2 billion at June 30, 2026, achieving a 17.5% year over year increase, which included 7.8% acquisition growth and 7.0% organic growth. Notably, Stantec's acquisition of Page contributed to over 40% backlog growth in its Buildings business. Additionally, organic growth was achieved in all regions, driven primarily by nearly 25% organic growth in its Global region and over 10% organic growth in its Water business. Contract backlog represents approximately 13 months of work. Cash flows from operations were $118.6 million, which was a decrease of $15.4 million compared to Q2 2025. This reflects required investment in net working capital as a result of revenue growth. Days sales outstanding (DSO) was 75 days, an increase of two days compared to Q2 2025 and within Stantec's target of 75 days. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA (on a trailing twelve-month basis) at June 30, 2026 remained at 1.3x, within Stantec's internal target range of 1.0x to 2.0x. On July 31, 2026 Stantec acquired Niche, a 200-person engineering and environmental consultancy firm in Australia, bolstering its Environmental Services operations. On August 12, 2026, Stantec's Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.245 per share, payable on October 15, 2026, to shareholders of record on September 29, 2026. Year-to-date Q2 2026 compared to year-to-date Q2 2025 Net revenue increased 10.3% or $325.2 million, to $3.5 billion, driven by acquisition growth of 7.2%, which primarily reflects strong results of Page in Stantec's US operations, and organic growth of 3.7%. Organic growth was driven by Stantec's Global region of 10.4% combined with modest growth in Canada and the United States. The largest driver of organic growth was a 13.0% increase in net revenue from Stantec's Water business. Project margin increased $176.6 million or 10.3%, to $1.9 billion. As a percentage of net revenue, project margin remained consistent with the prior year at 54.2%. Adjusted EBITDA increased $83.2 million or 15.5%, to $619.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin increased by 80 basis points over the prior period to 17.8%, primarily due to lower administrative and marketing expenses as a percentage of net revenue, reflecting Stantec's focus on efficient management of operations and optimization of discretionary spending. Net income increased 10.9% or $25.6 million, to $261.1 million, and diluted EPS increased 11.2%, or $0.23, to $2.29, mainly due to higher net revenue and lower administrative and marketing expenses as a percentage of net revenue partly offset by higher amortization of intangible assets and lease asset impairment. Adjusted net income grew 16.4% or $47.2 million, to $334.7 million, achieving 9.6% of net revenue—an increase of 50 basis points—and adjusted EPS increased 16.7%, or $0.42, to $2.94. Cash flows from operations were $116.3 million, a decrease of $118.4 million compared to the prior year. This reflects the required investment in net working capital as a result of revenue growth and the impacts of the Page integration in Q1 2026. body_text: View all news JetBlue BlueHouse™ Lounge at JFK Earns #1 in Newsweek’s Readers’ Choice™ Awards 2026 08/05/2026 Download (opens in new window) Consumer-voted recognition highlights thoughtful design, elevated amenities and a distinctly New York experience as BlueHouse, JFK named #1 ‘Best Airport Lounge 2026’ NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- JetBlue (NASDAQ: JBLU) today proudly announced its BlueHouse lounge at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) has been voted #1 ‘Best Airport Lounge’ in Newsweek’s Readers’ Choice™ Awards 2026, a consumer-voted program recognizing standout travel and hospitality experiences. BlueHouse at JFK is JetBlue’s first ever airport lounge, opened in December 2025. Photo courtesy of JetBlue. Located in JFK’s Terminal 5 – JetBlue’s flagship terminal – BlueHouse is a 9,000-square-foot, two-level lounge designed with an NYC apartment-style aesthetic, Art Deco details, curated artwork and playful nods to JetBlue’s history. The space offers fresh bites curated by Union Square Events, barista-made beverages and craft cocktails from New York partners including Joe Coffee, The Greats of Craft and Please Don’t Tell, as well as high-speed Wi-Fi, ample power outlets, open seating, quiet areas and a game room, giving customers space to socialize, work or relax before flying. “BlueHouse was never meant to feel like just another airport lounge. We designed it to feel more like a home—a place where customers can settle in, enjoy something delicious and start their journey before they even board,” said Stephanie Evans Greene, senior vice president of marketing and brand, JetBlue. “Inspired by the character and charm of New York, BlueHouse delivers a distinctly JetBlue welcome from the moment customers arrive. We’re thrilled that Newsweek readers named BlueHouse JFK the best airport lounge and incredibly proud of the teams and partners who brought that vision to life.” “Today’s travel experience is being redefined well before boarding—travelers now judge an airline by every hour of the journey, including the time spent on the ground,” said Ryan Kinney, Newsweek’s senior vice president, research, strategy, and revenue. “As JetBlue prepares to expand the BlueHouse experience to Boston, this recognition arrives at an especially meaningful moment. Newsweek’s Readers’ Choice™ Awards reflect the voices of readers who experience these brands firsthand, and in voting BlueHouse at JFK the #1 Best Airport Lounge, our readers delivered a powerful endorsement of JetBlue’s investment in the customer journey.” The recognition underscores JetBlue’s continued investment in elevating the customer experience, both on the ground and in the air, and comes as JetBlue prepares to open its second BlueHouse location in Boston’s Logan International Airport (BOS) Terminal C, later this summer, further expanding the airline’s lounge offering. Complimentary access to BlueHouse is available to eligible JetBlue TrueBlue® Mosaic 4 members, JetBlue Premier World Elite Mastercard ® cardmembers and transatlantic Mint® customers. For more information on BlueHouse, visit: jetblue.com/bluehouse . The Newsweek Readers’ Choice™ Awards recognize standout businesses, brands, and services across a wide range of consumer categories. Winners are determined through a public voting process in which readers select the companies and organizations they believe deliver exceptional quality, value, and customer experience. The 2026 program highlights leading companies across numerous industries, including the Travel category, where BlueHouse at JFK was recognized as #1 Best Airport Lounge. About JetBlue JetBlue is New York’s Hometown Airline® and a leading carrier in Boston, Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood, Los Angeles, Orlando, and San Juan. JetBlue carries customers to more than 100 destinations throughout the United States, Latin America, the Caribbean, Canada, and Europe. For more information and the best fares, visit jetblue.com . About Newsweek Newsweek is the global digital news organization built around the iconic 93-year-old American magazine. Newsweek reaches 100 million people monthly with its thought-provoking news, opinion, images, graphics, and video delivered across a dozen print and digital platforms. Headquartered in New York City, Newsweek also publishes international editions in EMEA and Asia. For more information, visit www.newsweek.com . body_text: View All News Pursuit Announces First Major Organic Growth Investment at Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa August 4, 2026 Three premium rainforest villas represent the first expansion since Pursuit acquired Tabacón in 2025, advancing the company's Vision 2030 growth strategy DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Pursuit Attractions and Hospitality, Inc. (NYSE: PRSU) today announced plans to develop three premium guest accommodation villas at Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa, representing the first major organic growth investment at Tabacón since acquiring the award-winning Costa Rican resort in July 2025. The expansion reflects Pursuit's Vision 2030 strategy of creating long-term shareholder value through disciplined organic growth investments that enhance market-leading guest experiences, alongside strategic acquisitions in iconic destinations. Located within Tabacón’s existing 570-acre resort property, the villas will help guests experience the resort at a deeper level and connect to Costa Rica's largest network of naturally flowing thermal springs, adjacent to the Arenal Volcano National Park protected rainforest reserve. With an anticipated opening in Summer 2027, each of the two-bedroom villas will span 2,250 square feet and feature a private plunge pool and an expansive outdoor terrace nestled within the rainforest. The expansion enhances Tabacón’s premium offering and long-term value proposition, reinforcing Pursuit’s position in Costa Rica as affluent travelers increasingly seek high-end, nature-based experiences. Leveraging the strong international demand driven by Tabacón’s renowned thermal river attraction, the new accommodation concept directly addresses evolving guest preferences while supporting future growth. Designed by acclaimed Costa Rican architecture firm Taller KEN, the villas embrace the same philosophy that has guided Tabacón since its founding: working with the rainforest rather than transforming it. Elevated on piles above the forest floor, the structures are designed to immerse guests in the sights, sounds and atmosphere of the surrounding landscape while minimizing their environmental footprint. “Tabacón is one of the world's great nature-based hospitality experiences, and this investment responds to growing guest demand by expanding premium accommodation capacity in a way that enhances an already exceptional guest experience," said David Barry, president and chief executive officer of Pursuit. "It's exactly how we intend to grow our experiences: making thoughtful investments in exceptional assets that strengthen the guest experience, increase the long-term value of our properties and support sustainable growth for our shareholders.” Barry added, "Just as importantly, we're committed to growing alongside the La Fortuna community and respecting the rainforest and thermal river that make Tabacón such an extraordinary place." "We're seeing growing demand from guests who want more than exceptional accommodations, they want to feel completely immersed in the destination," said Andrey Gómez, general manager of Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa. "These villas were created in response to that demand. They expand our premium offering while giving guests a more private, more personal way to experience the rainforest and thermal river that have made Tabacón one of Costa Rica's most iconic hospitality experiences." Guided by Tabacón's Legacy of Regeneration and Pursuit's Promise to Place, the project has been designed to respect the surrounding landscape while supporting the resort's long-standing commitment to environmental stewardship and community partnerships. Tabacón also holds Costa Rica's Certification for Sustainable Tourism at the Elite level, the country's highest designation, and is a founding member of the La Fortuna Sustainability Alliance. More information on Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa is available at tabacon.com About Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa Located within a 570-acre rainforest property at the base of Arenal Volcano, Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa is home to the only naturally flowing thermal river originating from the volcano. A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, Tabacón offers immersive hospitality where volcanic thermal waters, lush rainforest and personalized service come together in one of Costa Rica's most iconic natural settings. About Pursuit Pursuit Attractions and Hospitality, Inc. (NYSE: PRSU) is an attractions and hospitality company that owns and operates a collection of inspiring and unforgettable experiences in iconic destinations in the United States, Canada, Iceland and Costa Rica. title: Prologis Announces Responsible Data Center Development Commitments
summary: Data centers support the technology people and businesses rely on every day, from processing credit card payments to giving doctors digital access to patients’ medical records. As data center demand grows, communities and public officials are asking fair questions about power, water, local infrastructure and community benefits.
body_text: Introduction Data centers support the technology people and businesses rely on every day, from processing credit card payments to giving doctors digital access to patients’ medical records. As data center demand grows, communities and public officials are asking fair questions about power, water, local infrastructure and community benefits. For more than 40 years Prologis has invested with a clear focus on responsibility, reliability and long-term commitments to communities. We support clear, consistent and timely standards that help distinguish well-planned projects and give communities confidence in how growth is managed. To help communities understand who Prologis is as a developer and community partner, we published our Responsible Data Center Development Commitments , covering how we approach power planning, water use, environmental impact, community engagement, local benefits and accountability for every project. Content Above Blog Author 1. Protect ratepayers by planning and paying our fair share We will study power needs early, before a project moves too far in the development process. We will work with utilities, grid operators and public officials to identify the infrastructure needed to serve the project. Where upgrades are driven by our project, we will work through applicable utility processes to ensure those costs are identified and appropriately allocated, with the goal of protecting existing ratepayers. Related: Prologis recently signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge , which calls on large data center operators to fund the power generation and grid infrastructure their projects require rather than shifting those costs to existing ratepayers. 2. Use water responsibly We will evaluate local water conditions before advancing a project and design data centers to minimize water use. Our standard approach will prioritize closed-loop cooling systems that significantly reduce ongoing water demand. Where local conditions, customer requirements or technology needs call for a different approach, we will evaluate air-cooled, recycled water, non-potable water or other efficient solutions that reduce reliance on drinking water. We will explain our water approach in plain language during the local review process. Fast fact: Closed-loop cooling systems use roughly the same amount of water per building each day as a single car wash. 3. Be clear about backup power Data centers need backup power to operate reliably. We will explain how backup power is expected to be used, including testing, emissions controls and applicable permitting requirements. Where practical, we will evaluate cleaner or lower-impact options as technology and local infrastructure allow. 4. Reduce environmental impact We will evaluate greenhouse gas emissions and other environmental impacts as part of project planning. We will identify feasible ways to reduce those impacts through design innovation and engaging our customers and connect this work to Prologis’ goal to achieve net zero by 2040. We will be transparent about what can be addressed at the project level and what depends on broader energy infrastructure. Zoom in: We use whole-building life cycle assessments early in the development process to estimate greenhouse gas emissions associated with building materials and operations. Then, we find ways to reduce emissions through design and material choices. We also apply an internal carbon price to every project reviewed by our Investment Committee, ensuring carbon impacts are weighed alongside cost and performance. 5. Design with neighbors in mind We will plan sites with attention to the surrounding community. That includes using setbacks, screening, landscaping and building placement to reduce noise and visual impact. We will also manage construction activity with clear expectations for traffic, site access and working hours. 6. Regularly engage with communities We will continue to engage with elected officials and community members to share information, answer questions and understand local priorities. For major projects, we will provide public materials and a dedicated way for people to contact us. Community engagement should not start at the end of the process. Related: We weighed in Governor’s Abbott’s recent announcement for enhanced review of data center projects in Texas focused on grid reliability, ratepayer protections, water stewardship and community impacts. We support this measured path, which strengthens oversight while allowing investment and dialogue to continue. 7. Explain benefits clearly We will explain the expected local benefits of each major project in simple terms. That includes jobs, tax revenue and community investment. We will avoid inflated claims and focus on information that communities can understand and evaluate. By the numbers: The potential benefits can be significant: The Data Center Coalition reports that individual data centers generally support dozens to hundreds of direct jobs and employ hundreds of construction workers—sometimes more than 1,000 at peak construction. Nationally, a PwC analysis found that the U.S. data center industry contributed $204 billion in local, state and federal taxes in 2024. 8. Follow through on commitments For major data center projects, we will document the commitments we make during the development process. This may include commitments related to site design, traffic management, energy infrastructure, water use or community engagement. We will make it clear who is responsible for follow-through. When we commit to our communities, we deliver. For example, at International Park of Commerce in Tracy, California, we invested more than $250 million in surrounding infrastructure , including 31 lane miles of new roads, a new bridge, upgraded utilities, a 1-million-gallon water tank and a 30-acre public park. We took the same approach with our 2025 sustainability commitments. We set measurable goals, reported progress and delivered . And, we’re taking the same disciplined approach with data centers. To learn more about our approach visit https://www.prologis.com/real-estate/development/data-centers Chris Curtis Position Global Head of Data Centers, Prologis Chris Curtis serves as global head of data centers at Prologis. In addition, Chris serves on the Data Center Coalition Board and the Urban Land Institute (ULI) Data Center Product Council. A seasoned data center expert, Chris brings more than 5 gigawatts of data center development experience across the U.S., Canada and Europe. Before Prologis, Chris co-founded Compass Datacenters, where he led all development projects from 2011 to 2023. Prior to that, he spent a decade developing high-security, build-to-suit projects for U.S. Federal Government agencies. title: Senate Approves Dr. Erica Schwartz as New CDC Director Nominee Under Trump Administration
summary: Dr. Erica Schwartz Confirmed to Lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention After Senate Vote The United States Senate has confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as the next director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), placing her at the helm of one of the nation’s most important public health agencies. body_text: Dr. Erica Schwartz Confirmed to Lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention After Senate Vote The United States Senate has confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as the next director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), placing her at the helm of one of the nation’s most important public health agencies. The confirmation marks another major leadership transition for the CDC under President Donald Trump’s administration. The Senate voted 51 to 43 in favor of Schwartz’s appointment on August 5, 2026. Republican senators supported her confirmation, with Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia joining them in voting yes. Senators who voted against the nomination were Democrats and independent lawmakers who caucus with Democrats. Six senators did not participate in the vote, including Republican Senator Ron Johnson of Wisconsin and Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego of Arizona. With her confirmation, Schwartz becomes the second individual nominated by President Trump to serve as CDC director. Her appointment comes after previous leadership changes at the agency and ongoing discussions about the future direction of federal health policy. Who Is Dr. Erica Schwartz? Dr. Erica Schwartz brings extensive medical and public service experience to her new role. During President Trump’s first administration, she served as deputy surgeon general. She also previously held the position of chief medical officer for the United States Coast Guard. Throughout her career, Schwartz has worked in areas involving public health, emergency response, and healthcare leadership. Her background in government medical roles has been cited by supporters as a reason she is prepared to manage the CDC, which employs approximately 12,000 people and oversees programs focused on disease prevention, health research, and public safety. During her Senate confirmation hearing, Schwartz addressed several major public health issues, including vaccines and medical research. She stated that she believes vaccines are safe and effective and expressed support for vaccines using messenger RNA, commonly known as mRNA technology. Her comments were closely watched because some officials within the Trump administration, including Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., have previously raised concerns about certain vaccine policies and recommendations. CDC Leadership Changes and Recent Controversies Schwartz’s appointment follows a period of significant change at the CDC. In 2025, the Senate confirmed Susan Monarez as CDC director. However, President Trump removed Monarez from the position after approximately one month. The leadership dispute involved disagreements between Monarez and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. regarding recommendations from the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel. Monarez said Kennedy pressured her to accept vaccine guidance without changes, while Kennedy argued that Monarez was unwilling to consider revisions to the recommendations. The disagreement became part of a larger national debate about vaccine policy, government health guidance, and the role of scientific advisory committees. Following those events, Kennedy and the acting CDC director made changes to childhood vaccination recommendations in early 2026. The decision was partly based on advice from a vaccine advisory panel. However, a federal judge later blocked the update, ruling that many members of the panel had not been properly selected under federal procedures. The case remains under appeal. Schwartz Addresses Vaccine Policy During Confirmation Hearing One of the most closely examined parts of Schwartz’s confirmation hearing involved her views on vaccines. Lawmakers questioned her position on immunization policies and whether she would maintain scientific independence while serving under the current administration. Schwartz told senators that she supports vaccines and believes mRNA vaccine technology has an important role in modern medicine. Her position appeared to reassure some lawmakers who had previously expressed concerns about health-related nominations. Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, a physician and Republican member of the Senate, said he became confident in Schwartz’s ability to lead the CDC after reviewing her testimony and speaking with people familiar with her work. Cassidy said he believed Schwartz understood the responsibilities of the position and would be willing to challenge officials when necessary. What Schwartz’s Appointment Means for the CDC The CDC plays a central role in protecting public health in the United States. The agency monitors disease outbreaks, conducts scientific research, provides health recommendations, and supports state and local health departments. As CDC director, Schwartz will face several challenges, including rebuilding public trust, managing infectious disease threats, addressing vaccine debates, and overseeing a large federal workforce. Public health experts and lawmakers will closely monitor how she balances administration priorities with scientific recommendations. The CDC director position requires cooperation with federal health officials, medical professionals, researchers, and communities across the country. Schwartz’s leadership approach will likely influence how the agency communicates health information and responds to future public health emergencies. Political Reaction to the Confirmation The Senate vote reflected continued political divisions surrounding public health leadership. While Republicans largely supported Schwartz’s nomination, most Democratic lawmakers opposed it. Supporters argued that Schwartz’s government experience and medical background make her qualified for the role. Critics raised concerns connected to broader disagreements over the Trump administration’s approach to health policy. The confirmation highlights the ongoing national discussion about the relationship between politics, science, and public health decision-making. Looking Ahead Dr. Erica Schwartz is expected to begin leading the CDC during a period of major transition. Her ability to work with different groups, communicate scientific information clearly, and manage internal agency challenges will shape her tenure. The CDC remains a key institution responsible for protecting Americans from health threats. Under Schwartz’s leadership, the agency will continue to face questions about vaccines, disease prevention strategies, and public confidence in government health guidance. As she takes on the role, attention will remain focused on how she navigates scientific priorities, administrative goals, and the expectations of lawmakers and the American public. Sources The Epoch Times report, published August 5, 2026. U.S. Senate confirmation records and public statements from lawmakers regarding the nomination. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention official information about agency responsibilities and public health programs. Readers should consult official government sources and multiple news outlets for additional information and context.

title: Disney Legends in Conversation: Susan Egan
summary: Susan Egan is an actress best known for originating the role of Belle in Broadway's 'Beauty and the Beast' and voicing Megara in 'Hercules.'
body_text: Disney Legends in Conversation: Susan Egan Entertainment August 7, 2026 8 min. read The Disney Legends Award ceremony will mark the final day of D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event presented by Visa® , a one-of-a-kind, multi-day fan experience showcasing the very best in creative storytelling and innovation from across the worlds of Disney. Hosted by Ryan Seacrest , the event will be filled with tributes and unforgettable moments to honor and celebrate the icons behind the magic who have made a lasting impact on Disney. This year, The Walt Disney Company’s highest honor will be presented to 13 individuals — Chris Berman , Jerry Bruckheimer , Susan Egan , Eric Goldberg , Anne Hathaway , Bob Iger , Kim Irvine , Dwayne Johnson , the Jonas Brothers , Lin‑Manuel Miranda , and Alan Tudyk — who for generations have defined Disney across entertainment, storytelling, and experiences. In an exclusive Q&A, Susan Egan — who is being recognized in the Voice category — reflects on her contributions to the company and what it means to be named a Disney Legend. How does it feel to be honored as a Disney legend? Being honored as a Disney Legend is so completely humbling. But also, I’m just thrilled to get to be part a small part of Walt Disney’s legacy. I feel like I already won just by getting to be a part of so many of these projects over the last 30 years, so I’m thrilled and humbled. What are some of your earliest memories of Disney? I laugh because kids today have streaming services. They have all these films on demand. I didn’t have that. I grew up in the ’70s and early ’80s when Disney would rerelease movies every once in a while. Of course, I loved Cinderella . I had my little 45 Cinderella record, and I dreamed of having a dress like that. I get emotional thinking about it, having no idea that someday I would get a dress like that, only mine was in yellow and I got to wear it eight shows a week [as Belle in Beauty and the Beast on Broadway ]. It was pretty thrilling. I grew up about 15 minutes away from Disneyland , and my mom would take us to the park once a year — on a school day, typically, so that we would have shorter lines, because she loved roller coasters, too. And I would go with my older brother and sister, and we always had the best time — never dreaming that it would actually be a career option to work for this company, and especially for so many years. Dreams come true. ‘Beauty and the Beast’ on Broadway You originated the role of Belle in Beauty and the Beast on Broadway , earning a Tony Award® nomination for Best Actress. What did that role and experience mean to you? Playing Belle in Beauty and the Beast was a little bit of life imitating art. I had just moved to New York City; I think my reaction to Times Square was probably pretty similar to Belle’s reaction to the enchanted castle! I was also surrounded by such truly magical people, as clichéd as that sounds. Terrence Mann, who was the Beast; Gary Beach , who was Lumière, the light of our production; and Beth Fowler, [who was Mrs. Potts] — those are the people who formed who I became as an artist. They were such great role models, and they took such good care of me. And they taught me lessons when I needed to learn them. I will forever be grateful to that experience. Cast and crew at the ‘Hercules’ world premiere in Times Square Megara in ‘Hercules’ Your Hercules character, Megara, has a real cult following. Why do you think that is? Meg was a little before her time . She is spicy. She is not a Disney Princess — which people like to remind me constantly , but I’m good with it. She has a past, and I think that’s what made her relatable. She was valuable. She made poor choices. And Meg’s storyline shows you that it’s never too late to make a different choice to open your heart, to be vulnerable, and to understand that love is transformative. I think it was her humanity that made her kind of a cult favorite. And, definitely, [it was] John [Musker ] and Ron [Clements ]’ script. I wish in real life I had the comebacks that Meg has! She always knew exactly what to say. Mickey Mouse; Minnie Mouse; Disney Legend Susan Egan; Josh D’Amaro, CEO of the Walt Disney Company; and Joe Schott, President of Disney Signature Experiences, attend the ‘Disney Destiny’ christening in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. What was your reaction to being named a godmother of the Disney Destiny ship? I got a phone call… to tell me that I was going to be the godmother of the Disney Destiny . And I thought to myself, “How many people weren’t available that you would call me?” [Laughs.] I sat down on my kitchen floor and I cried. It’s such an honor. There are only a few ships — and I’ve been on every single one of them performing over the last 25 years — so I know how special that is. And the Destiny in particular, a heroes- and villain-themed ship… [has] Café Megara. And, of course, their live-action stage production of Hercules is the be all, end all. So, I was very, very excited. I am a proud godmother. She’s a pretty baby. What’s been the most rewarding part of producing so many Disney concerts and events over the years? I am forever grateful to Disney for allowing me to grow and have my own adventure — very similar to Belle — and for giving me the space to be creative in a new way. I love being behind the scenes. I love working with my partners at Disney Concerts to create live events around the world. Not everybody is lucky enough to grow up 15 minutes from Disneyland, or to see a Disney Broadway show. We get to bring this music, these characters, and these film clips to live stages, sometimes with full orchestras and phenomenal singers. I’ve literally traveled the world three or four times now, all through Asia, through the Middle East, through Australia, New Zealand, Europe, London — I mean, all over the place . [I’ve traveled] the U.S., a couple of times. And sharing this material with audiences around the world really gives you the insight that Disney is a unifier. It is a common denominator amongst humans on this planet, because everybody, everywhere sings along to “Let It Go.” Go the Distance Watch Now Hercules must go from zero to hero to save the world from Hades. 1997 Streaming on Disney+ Is there anything else you want to say about Disney in general — how it makes you feel, either as a fan or as someone who has contributed so much to its larger legacy? Disney, of course, was part of my childhood, particularly as somebody who grew up in Southern California. The films — the whole renaissance of [animated] moviemaking — happened when I was in college. And being such a fan of musical theater, I was so blown away by the films like The Little Mermaid and Beauty and the Beast and Aladdin . These were celebrations of a truly American art form on film. And then to get to be a part of that as an artist was truly thrilling because long after I’m gone, these projects will last. My kids will see it. Their kids will see it. I never take that for granted. But I think my favorite part is what I’m getting to do now, where I get to bring new talent into the family and share with them that once you’re in this family, you’re forever in this family. This family is beautiful. To be a part of that, and to get to travel the world and sing this music for audiences all over the place, it’s taken what I was able to do 30 years ago, and now it’s just amplified even larger. I feel like the luckiest girl in the world. It’s the truth. About the Disney Legends Program The Disney Legends Awards program is a 39-year tradition of The Walt Disney Company, which began when Fred MacMurray was honored in 1987. Including this year’s honorees, a total of 329 Disney Legends has been named. Past Disney Legends include Tim Allen , Julie Andrews , Angela Bassett , Tony Baxter , Kristen Bell , James Cameron , Jamie Lee Curtis , Miley Cyrus , Marc Davis , Robert Downey Jr. , Harrison Ford , Annette Funicello , Josh Gad , Whoopi Goldberg , Jonathan Groff , Steve Jobs , Elton John , Angela Lansbury , Stan Lee , George Lucas , Steve Martin , Burny Mattinson , Alan Menken , Idina Menzel , Hayley Mills , Fess Parker , Ellen Pompeo , Robin Roberts , the Sherman Brothers , Marty Sklar , Dick Van Dyke , Barbara Walters , Betty White , John Williams , Robin Williams , and Oprah Winfrey . title: ProMIS Neurosciences Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Highlights
summary: Announced positive blinded six-month interim safety and biomarker results from PRECISE-AD, the Company's Phase 1b trial of PMN310 in…...
body_text: ProMIS Neurosciences Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Highlights Aug 13, 2026 Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q Filing PDF HTML XBRL ZIP HTML Announced positive blinded six-month interim safety and biomarker results from PRECISE-AD, the Company's Phase 1b trial of PMN310 in patients with early Alzheimer's disease (AD), including zero cases of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities-edema (ARIA-E) across all participants and genotypes, including APOE4 homozygotes. Observed early, directionally consistent declines in two complementary biomarkers, plasma pTau217 and CSF MTBR-tau243, in a blinded analysis pooling both active- and placebo-treated patients under the trial’s ongoing 3-to-1 randomization. The second quarter ended with $53.4 million in cash and short-term investments, which is expected to fund operations through 2027, beyond the Company’s anticipated 12-month topline PRECISE-AD readout expected in the first quarter of 2027. Cambridge, Massachusetts, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. (Nasdaq: PMN), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the generation and development of antibody therapeutics targeting toxic misfolded proteins in neurodegenerative diseases, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update. “The second quarter of 2026 was a pivotal period for ProMIS, as we continued to advance PRECISE-AD while maintaining a strong financial position,” said Neil Warma, President and Chief Executive Officer of ProMIS Neurosciences. “We ended the quarter with $53.4 million in cash and short-term investments, providing runway through 2027, beyond our next major anticipated catalyst.” “Subsequent to quarter end, on July 28th, we announced positive blinded six-month interim safety and biomarker results from PRECISE-AD, our Phase 1b trial of PMN310 in patients with early AD. Across all 136 safety-evaluable participants and APOE genotypes, we observed no cases of ARIA-E. We also observed an early and directionally consistent movement in plasma pTau217 and CSF MTBR-tau243 in the blinded analysis, which pooled active and placebo-treated patients.” “We believe these data reinforce the thesis behind PMN310: that selectively targeting toxic amyloid-beta oligomers and avoiding plaque may offer a path to amyloid-directed therapy with a significantly improved safety profile, including a substantially reduced ARIA burden, and a potential for improved efficacy. We look forward to the 12-month unblinded topline results from PRECISE-AD, expected in the first quarter of 2027, which will include cognitive outcomes, and we believe will represent an important next step in evaluating PMN310’s potential for patients with early AD.” Corporate Highlights Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) Program (PMN310) — PRECISE-AD Interim Data PRECISE-AD is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1b trial evaluating PMN310 in patients with mild cognitive impairment due to early AD. The trial completed enrollment in December 2025 with 144 subjects across 22 U.S. sites, randomized 3-to-1 to active drug versus placebo across three different dose cohorts (5, 10, and 20 mg/kg), dosed monthly by intravenous infusion over 12 months. The evaluable number of patients in the interim analysis was 136 of the 144 enrolled. The population was genetically and demographically representative: mean age of 73.3 years, 58% female, and 61% carrying at least one APOE4 allele, including 11% APOE4 homozygotes, the population at highest risk of ARIA with plaque-binding antibodies. As of the July 22, 2026 data cutoff date, all 136 safety-evaluable patients had been dosed for at least six months, 78% for at least nine months, and 49% had completed the full 12 months of dosing. Safety: The interim data demonstrated a favorable safety profile across all genotypes, including APOE4 homozygotes. There were no cases of ARIA-E and a 4.4% incidence of total ARIA (all mild and asymptomatic, consisting of only amyloid-related imaging abnormalities -microhemorrhages (ARIA-H)), with no treatment-related serious adverse events and no drug-related discontinuations at the interim. Biomarkers: In the blinded, pooled analysis, plasma pTau217 declined approximately 15% from baseline through Day 169, with roughly 68.5% of patients showing a decline, and CSF MTBR-tau243 declined approximately 13.3%, with approximately 62.5% of patients showing a decline. Both the direction and proportion of patients showing a favorable response are broadly consistent with the trial’s 75% active-drug allocation. The trial remains blinded and ongoing. The Company expects all patients to complete 12-month dosing by the fourth quarter of 2026 and, following database lock and statistical analysis, to report unblinded 12-month topline data, including the full safety dataset, an expanded biomarker panel, and clinical cognitive outcome measures, in the first quarter of 2027. Pipeline Progress and Scientific Presentations PMN267 (ALS/FTD): The Company’s program targeting misfolded TDP-43 has been humanized in a human IgG1 framework and is progressing through investigational new drug (IND)-enabling studies. PMN442 (Parkinson’s Disease, Dementia with Lewy Bodies, Multiple System Atrophy): The Company’s lead candidate targeting pathogenic alpha-synuclein has been humanized and is advancing toward IND-enabling studies based on its selective binding activity. The Company presented a poster at the 2026 Alzheimer’s Association International Conference (AAIC) highlighting the first human evidence of amyloid-beta oligomer target engagement and removal by PMN310. Corporate and Investor Activities Mr. Warma presented at multiple investor conferences during the quarter, including the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference, the Wolfe Research R&D Day focused on Alzheimer’s disease, and the H.C. Wainwright Neuro Perspectives Expert Summit. An additional four research firms initiated coverage of ProMIS during the quarter: Cantor Fitzgerald, Roth Capital, Brookline Capital Markets, and Chardan Capital Markets. ProMIS hosted a live webinar to share the interim blinded data results with two independent key opinion leaders, Dr. Will Mantyh of the University of Minnesota and Dr. Michael Weiner of University of California San Francisco, who offered their perspective on the data and its clinical relevance. Future Activities and Upcoming Milestones Participation and presentations at multiple investor and medical conferences, including Clinical Trials on AD (CTAD) Presentation of unblinded 12-month topline data from PRECISE-AD, anticipated in the first quarter of 2027. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Cash Position: As of June 30, 2026, the Company’s cash and short-term investments were $53.4 million, compared to $6.1 million as of December 31, 2025. The increase primarily reflects $70.1 million in net proceeds received in January 2026 from a private placement financing in which certain of the Company’s own directors and management participated alongside external investors. Cash Runway: Based on the current operating plan, existing cash resources are expected to fund planned operations through 2027, beyond the anticipated 12-month topline readout from PRECISE-AD expected in Q1 2027. Net Loss: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $11.7 million, or $1.28 per share, compared to a net loss of $10.1 million, or $7.26 per share, for the same period in 2025. The improvement in loss per share reflects the increase in weighted-average shares outstanding following the January 2026 financing. About ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. ProMIS Neurosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to the discovery and development of therapeutic antibodies and vaccines selective for toxic oligomers associated with the development and progression of neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases. The Company’s proprietary target discovery engine, EpiSelect™, has been shown to predict novel targets known as Disease Specific Epitopes (DSEs) on the molecular surface of misfolded proteins that cause neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and Parkinson’s Disease (PD). ProMIS has offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts (USA) and Toronto, Ontario (CAN). About PMN310 and the PRECISE-AD Trial for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) PMN310, the Company’s lead product candidate for the treatment of AD, is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody designed to selectively target toxic oligomers while avoiding plaque, thereby potentially reducing or eliminating amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) liability. Because PMN310 may not be limited by off-target binding or side effects, it could potentially offer an improved efficacy profile over other amyloid-directed antibody therapeutics. PMN310 was granted Fast Track designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in July 2025. PRECISE-AD (NCT06750432) is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1b study evaluating the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of multiple ascending doses (5, 10, 20 mg/kg) of intravenous PMN310 in patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment due to AD or mild AD (Stage 3 and Stage 4 AD). PRECISE-AD is the first study to examine the effects of a monoclonal antibody directed solely against Aβ oligomers on biomarkers associated with AD pathology and clinical outcomes. Safety is a primary outcome of the study, with particular emphasis on assessing whether, as a non-plaque binder, PMN310 may have a reduced risk of ARIA. The study is powered to provide 95% confidence for detection of ARIA and is designed to provide meaningful insight into the effects of PMN310 on biomarkers and clinical outcomes. EpiSelect™ Drug Discovery Engine Toxic misfolded proteins underlie the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease (PD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Generation of therapeutic antibodies selectively targeting only disease-misfolded protein isoforms, while sparing normal or irrelevant isoforms of the same protein, has not yet been successfully achieved by conventional immunization strategies. ProMIS Neurosciences has developed a computational platform (EpiSelect™) to identify conformational epitopes that are uniquely exposed on toxic misfolded proteins, which can then be used to generate misfolding-specific antibodies or vaccine formulations. Unlike basic chatbots, these agents understand request intent, reference knowledge bases accurately, and trigger backend workflows when appropriate. How does conversational ticketing differ from traditional ticketing systems? Traditional systems require employees to navigate portals, fill out forms, and select categories before submitting requests. Conversational ticketing lets employees describe needs in natural language within familiar tools like Slack while the system handles categorization, routing, and tracking automatically. title: How to Calculate Payroll Gross to Net in 5 Procedures for Payroll and HR Administrators
summary: Payroll math itself rarely breaks. What breaks, almost every time, is the order things happen in, or the classification applied to a bonus, a deduction code, or a rounding rule. A time punch gets converted incorrectly. A 401(k) deferral gets…
body_text: Payroll math itself rarely breaks. What breaks, almost every time, is the order things happen in, or the classification applied to a bonus, a deduction code, or a rounding rule. A time punch gets converted incorrectly. A 401(k) deferral gets applied after tax instead of before it. A non-discretionary bonus gets left out of the regular rate used for overtime. None of these are calculation errors in the strict sense. They are sequencing and classification errors, and they compound quietly across pay cycles until an agency notice or a payroll correction forces the issue. This is the procedure layer for growth-stage payroll and HR teams: five ordered steps that take a company from raw time data to a validated net pay figure, in the sequence a payroll administrator actually executes them each pay cycle. This guide assumes you already know what gross pay, taxable wages, and pre-tax deductions mean. It focuses on the order of operations: what has to be confirmed before the next step starts, and where standardization breaks down as headcount, states, and pay complexity grow past the point where a spreadsheet and institutional memory were enough. Growing companies don't have to choose between running this sequence themselves and handing it off entirely. AsureCentral gives a payroll or HR administrator the same five-step process laid out below, built into one connected system, from time capture through net pay validation. Teams that would rather hand execution to a specialist can move that exact sequence to AsureWorks, Asure's managed payroll service and PEO alternative, on the same platform, without a data migration or a change to the underlying pay rules, and with the client remaining the employer of record throughout. Time and Compensation Inputs How to Capture and Round Employee Time for Payroll How to Capture and Round Employee Time for Payroll is the procedure for turning raw clock-in and clock-out records into a finalized, auditable time register before any pay calculation begins. It's executed by a payroll or HR administrator at the close of each pay period and produces a locked time register split into regular and potential overtime hours. Use it whenever your workforce includes hourly or mixed-compensation employees. Prerequisites: Export clock-in and clock-out records for every hourly employee across the full pay period Confirm a documented rounding policy, approved by HR or legal, is on file Verify each employee's pay classification, hourly or salaried, for the period Have federal and applicable state overtime threshold rules on hand Ordered steps: Export the raw punches. Pull every clock-in and clock-out record for the full pay period from your time-tracking system. Apply the rounding policy. Round each punch to the increment your documented policy defines, and confirm the convention averages out neutrally over time rather than consistently rounding in the employer's favor. Convert minutes to decimal hours. Divide remaining minutes by 60. Twenty minutes becomes 0.33 hours, not 0.20. Entering it as "0.20" understates that day's pay. Total each workday. Add the decimal-hour entries within a single workday to produce a daily hours figure per employee. Total the workweek. Aggregate daily hours into a rolling seven-day workweek, since federal overtime is measured weekly, not by pay period. Flag exceptions. Route missing punches, duplicate entries, or any day exceeding 24 hours to the employee's manager for correction before the register locks. Lock and archive the register. Finalize the corrected time register in your payroll system and retain the source punch data per your record retention practice. Expected outcome: a locked, auditable time register showing decimal hours per employee, split into regular and potential overtime hours, ready to feed gross pay computation. Use this every pay period for hourly or mixed-compensation employees. Skip it for salaried-exempt employees, whose pay isn't calculated from hours worked. Common pitfalls: rounding that only favors the employer, rounding down on late arrivals but never on early departures, creates unpaid-wage exposure. The convention has to cut both ways. And skipping the decimal conversion, entering "1:20" as 1.20 hours instead of 1.33, looks minor but compounds across every pay period an employee works that shift pattern. Teams that run this procedure inside AsureCentral get the rounding policy and the resulting time register in the same environment that computes gross pay next, so nothing has to be re-entered into a second system. Employers who hand time review to AsureWorks get a payroll specialist checking the register for the same exceptions before it moves to the next procedure. How to Compute Gross Pay by Pay Frequency How to Compute Gross Pay by Pay Frequency is the procedure for converting each employee's compensation rate into the correct gross pay figure for the current pay period, accounting for pay frequency differences across a workforce. It's executed by a payroll administrator immediately after the time register is finalized and produces a gross pay figure per employee. Use it every pay cycle, particularly when hourly and salaried employees are paid on different schedules. Prerequisites: Confirm the finalized time register from the time capture procedure for hourly employees Verify each employee's current annual salary or hourly rate against the HR system of record Document the pay frequency for each employee group (weekly equals 52 periods a year, biweekly 26, semi-monthly 24, monthly 12) Identify any mid-period rate changes, new hires, or terminations that require proration Ordered steps: Identify pay frequency per group. Confirm whether each employee group is paid weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, or monthly from the payroll schedule. Calculate the salaried period rate. Divide annual salary by pay periods per year. A $65,000 salary paid semi-monthly is $65,000 divided by 24, or $2,708.33 per period. Calculate hourly gross. Multiply regular decimal hours from the time register by the hourly rate. Thirty eight and one-third hours at $22 an hour produces $843.26 in regular gross pay. Prorate partial periods. For a new hire or termination mid-period, divide the period rate by the calendar or working days in the period, then multiply by days actually worked. Add confirmed supplemental earnings. Include any approved commissions, bonuses, or shift differentials for the period as a separate line. These get layered with overtime in the next procedure, not folded in here. Record gross pay per employee. Enter the resulting gross pay figure, broken into regular and supplemental earnings, into the payroll system before moving to deduction sequencing. Expected outcome: a gross pay figure per employee, itemized into regular and supplemental earnings, ready for deduction sequencing. Run this every cycle for every employee type. If someone has both a salary and hourly overtime component, compute each piece separately, then add them together. AsureCentral applies pay frequency conversion across weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, and monthly schedules within the same system that produced the time register, so a mixed-frequency workforce doesn't require a side calculation. Teams that prefer AsureWorks to run this step get the same conversion performed by a payroll specialist, against the same underlying pay rules. Deductions and Variable Pay How to Sequence Pre- and Post-Tax Deductions How to Sequence Pre- and Post-Tax Deductions is the procedure for applying benefit elections and required withholding in the correct order, pre-tax deductions first, then tax withholding, then post-tax deductions, to produce an accurate taxable wage figure and net pay. It's executed by a payroll administrator once gross pay is confirmed and produces a deduction ledger per employee. Use it every pay cycle in which an employee has any benefit election or withholding obligation. Prerequisites: Confirm the gross pay figure per employee from the prior procedure Pull current benefit election records (401(k) deferral percentage, health and dental premiums, FSA or HSA contributions, commuter benefits) Gather any garnishment or court-ordered deduction notices with per-period amounts and priority rankings Have current federal and state withholding tables on hand Confirm each employee's W-4 and state withholding form is on file Ordered steps: List every deduction type. Compile pre-tax benefit contributions, tax withholdings, and post-tax deductions into a single ledger row per employee. Apply pre-tax deductions first. Subtract Section 125 premiums, 401(k) or 403(b) deferrals, and FSA or HSA contributions from gross pay. A traditional 401(k) contribution reduces the federal income tax base, but it does not reduce the Social Security and Medicare (FICA) taxable wage base. These are two separate figures, not one blended number, and treating them as the same is one of the most common sources of downstream withholding errors. Calculate federal withholding. Apply the wage-bracket or percentage method from IRS Publication 15 to the federal taxable wage figure, using the employee's W-4 filing status. Calculate FICA withholding. Withhold 6.2% for Social Security up to the 2026 wage base of $184,500, and 1.45% for Medicare with no wage base cap ( IRS Publication 15 ). Flag any employee approaching the Social Security wage base so withholding stops at the correct point. Calculate state and local withholding. Apply the applicable state table and any local tax rate to taxable wages using the employee's state withholding form. Apply post-tax deductions. Subtract Roth 401(k) contributions, after-tax life insurance, wage garnishments, and payroll-deducted charitable gifts, in priority order. Garnishments generally carry statutory priority over voluntary deductions. Validate deduction totals. Confirm total deductions don't exceed net pay. If they do, apply the legally required priority order and document the shortfall rather than silently underpaying a lower-priority deduction. Record the deduction ledger. Enter each line item with its deduction code, amount, and pre-tax or post-tax classification, for the pay stub and tax filing. Expected outcome: a complete deduction ledger per employee, showing both taxable wage figures and every withholding line item, ready for net pay computation and pay stub generation. Use this every cycle for anyone with an election or withholding obligation. If an employee genuinely has none, which is rare, move directly from gross pay to net pay validation. Common pitfalls: applying a 401(k) deferral after tax overstates the employee's federal taxable wages and understates take-home pay, since traditional 401(k) contributions are pre-tax for federal income tax purposes. And garnishment priority isn't uniform. A federal tax levy can outrank a child support order in some jurisdictions, and ordinary creditor garnishments are capped at a different share of disposable earnings than support orders. Confirm the applicable priority order before sequencing multiple garnishments for the same employee. Teams that hand this procedure to AsureWorks get a payroll specialist checking deduction sequencing as part of the managed service's ongoing payroll administration, rather than running the check themselves each cycle. Teams running this procedure themselves inside AsureCentral work from the same benefit election and W-4 data the platform already holds, so there's no separate file to reconcile against. How to Layer Overtime and Variable Compensation into Payroll Calculations How to Layer Overtime and Variable Compensation into Payroll Calculations is the procedure for computing overtime premiums, bonuses, and commissions, and folding them into the gross-to-net calculation without distorting tax withholding or deduction amounts. It's executed by a payroll administrator whenever a non-exempt employee works overtime or receives variable pay in the period, and produces an adjusted gross pay figure. Use it any period that includes overtime hours, a bonus, or a commission payment. Prerequisites: Confirm weekly hours totals from the finalized time register, with regular and overtime hours already separated Confirm each affected employee's regular rate of pay, including any non-discretionary bonus that must be folded in Have approved bonus or commission amounts for the period, classified as discretionary or non-discretionary Check state overtime rules, since some states require daily overtime in addition to the federal weekly threshold Ordered steps: Identify overtime-eligible hours. From the time register, isolate hours worked beyond 40 in the workweek for each non-exempt employee. Federal law requires overtime pay of at least 1.5 times the regular rate for hours beyond 40 in a workweek ( 29 U.S.C. Section 207 ). Some states add a daily threshold. California, for example, requires 1.5 times the regular rate beyond eight hours in a single workday and double time beyond 12 hours ( California Department of Industrial Relations ). Calculate the true regular rate. If the employee received a non-discretionary bonus or commission this period, add it to straight-time earnings and divide by total hours worked. This produces the regular rate the overtime premium is based on, not just the stated hourly wage. Compute the overtime premium. Multiply overtime-eligible hours by half the regular rate. Straight-time pay for those hours is already counted in the regular-rate calculation above, so only the additional half applies here. Add discretionary bonuses separately. Enter approved discretionary bonuses as their own earnings line. They don't affect the regular rate calculation, but they are subject to supplemental withholding. Add commissions. Add confirmed commission amounts as supplemental wages. The federal flat supplemental withholding rate is 22% for supplemental wages up to $1 million in the calendar year, and 37% above that threshold ( IRS Publication 15 ), or the employer can aggregate commissions with regular wages under the employee's W-4 election. Recalculate gross pay. Sum regular earnings, the overtime premium, non-discretionary bonus, discretionary bonus, and commissions into the final adjusted gross pay figure. Pass the adjusted figure forward. Enter adjusted gross pay into the deduction ledger from the prior procedure. Deductions and withholding apply to this final figure, not the pre-overtime amount. Expected outcome: an adjusted gross pay figure, itemized by earnings component, ready for the pay stub and tax filing. Use this whenever a non-exempt employee exceeds 40 hours in a workweek or receives a bonus or commission. Don't apply an overtime premium to salaried-exempt employees classified under FLSA exemptions. Administrators running this step inside AsureCentral apply overtime and bonus calculations against the same time register and pay rules used in the earlier procedures, with no separate spreadsheet. Employers who hand this step to AsureWorks get a payroll specialist checking the regular-rate math, the area practitioners most often get wrong when a non-discretionary bonus is in play. Net Pay Output and Validation How to Validate Net Pay Before Disbursement How to Validate Net Pay Before Disbursement is the procedure for confirming that every employee's net pay figure is mathematically correct and consistent with the prior period before payroll is submitted or direct deposit is initiated. It's executed by a payroll administrator or finance ops lead as the final pre-disbursement control and produces a validated payroll register . Use it before every disbursement, without exception. Prerequisites: Complete the deduction ledger per employee from the deduction sequencing procedure, with adjusted gross pay from the overtime procedure where it applies Pull the prior period's payroll register for comparison Generate your payroll system's pre-processing gross-to-net report, or complete the calculation manually Define a variance threshold for manual review, for example, flagging any net pay change greater than 15% from the prior period Ordered steps: Generate the pre-disbursement register. Produce a full register showing gross pay, every deduction, and net pay per employee. Verify the math on a sample. For three to five employees, or all employees if the team is under 20, manually recalculate that gross pay minus pre-tax deductions equals taxable wages, and taxable wages minus withholding minus post-tax deductions equals net pay. Compare to the prior period. Flag any employee whose net pay differs from the prior period by more than your variance threshold, and document why (a new deduction, a rate change, overtime, and so on). Confirm new-hire and termination accuracy. Verify new hires appear with correct start-date proration, and that terminated employees appear only if a final paycheck is due. Validate employer tax liability. Confirm employer-side FICA is correctly calculated (6.2% Social Security up to the $184,500 wage base, plus 1.45% Medicare with no cap) and that FUTA is correctly calculated, 6.0% on the first $7,000 per employee, reduced to an effective 0.6% for employers current on state unemployment tax, for the period's tax deposit ( IRS Publication 15 ). Approve and lock. Obtain the required approval, lock the register against further edits, and submit for disbursement. Expected outcome: a locked, approved payroll register with documented variance explanations and a confirmed employer tax liability figure for the period. Use this before every disbursement without exception. If the variance review surfaces an error after the lock deadline, follow your payroll provider's off-cycle correction procedure rather than proceeding with a known error. Common pitfalls: skipping the prior-period comparison catches formula errors but misses the systematic kind, like a deduction that silently stopped applying, which compounds quietly across cycles. And approving under time pressure without the manual sample check is one of the more common ways an avoidable payroll error reaches an employee's paycheck. Teams running this control inside AsureCentral get the prior period's register and the current one in the same system, so the comparison in step three doesn't require exporting two separate reports. Employers using AsureWorks get this same six-point review performed by a payroll specialist before every disbursement, against the same underlying pay rules the team would otherwise apply itself. How to Sequence These Procedures Each Pay Cycle Run these five procedures in the same order every pay cycle. Each one depends on the output of the one before it. Start with time capture and rounding if your workforce includes any hourly or mixed-compensation employees. A salaried-only team can start directly at gross pay computation, since there's no time register to build. Run overtime and variable pay layering only in periods when overtime was actually worked or variable compensation was approved. If neither applies, pass the gross pay figure from the pay frequency procedure straight into deduction sequencing. Always end with net pay validation before disbursement, regardless of team size or the software you use to get there. If you're standing up payroll for the first time, run all five procedures on a parallel test payroll before processing anything live. Calculation discrepancies in a new setup are most likely to surface, and be caught, during that testing and validation window, not after the first live paycheck has already gone out. That's the point of running the sequence in parallel: it turns a configuration mistake into a correction on paper instead of a correction on someone's paycheck. Why Net Pay Validation Is Your Highest-Leverage Control Of the five procedures above, net pay validation carries the most weight. Most payroll errors that reach this stage aren't calculation mistakes. They're sequencing mistakes, a deduction applied in the wrong order, classification mistakes, a discretionary bonus treated as non-discretionary or the reverse, or configuration mistakes, a new deduction code set up at the wrong rate or in the wrong pre-tax or post-tax bucket. A structured, six-point pre-disbursement review is what catches those before they reach an employee's paycheck or compound into a filing error at year-end. Standardizing this sequence now, before headcount, states, and pay complexity grow further, is what keeps that kind of drift from becoming an expensive correction later. Whether your team runs these five procedures manually, validates what your payroll software already produced, or wants Asure to run the sequence for you, the underlying steps don't change. That's the choice AsureCentral and AsureWorks are built to give a growing company. Run this exact five-step sequence yourself inside AsureCentral, with the time register, gross pay, deduction ledger, and payroll register living in one connected system, or hand the sequencing and validation to AsureWorks payroll specialists on that same platform, without migrating data or changing your underlying pay rules, while your business remains the employer of record throughout. Common Payroll Calculation Questions Is salary calculated based on 365 days or working days? For most salaried employees, gross pay comes from dividing annual salary by the number of pay periods in the year, 24 for semi-monthly or 26 for biweekly, not by 365 calendar days. The 365-day method applies only in specific situations, like prorating a partial year of salary for a new hire, where you divide the annual salary by 365 and multiply by days employed. What is 20 minutes expressed as payroll hours? Twenty minutes equals 0.33 decimal hours (20 divided by 60). Payroll always converts time to decimal hours before multiplying by an hourly rate. Entering "0:20" as 0.20 instead of 0.33 understates that day's pay by roughly 8 minutes of earnings. How does payroll software calculate taxes automatically? Payroll software applies the IRS wage-bracket or percentage method tables to each employee's taxable wages, gross pay minus pre-tax deductions, using the filing status and elections from the employee's W-4. State withholding uses the equivalent state table. The software automates the lookup. It doesn't validate whether the underlying W-4 data or pre-tax deduction classification is correct. That check is the administrator's responsibility, and it's exactly what the net pay validation procedure above is for. How do charitable payroll deductions work? Charitable payroll deductions are post-tax. They don't reduce an employee's taxable wages. The employer withholds the elected amount from net pay and remits it to the designated charity, and the employee may claim the deduction separately on a personal tax return. What are the four basic steps in calculating payroll? The four foundational steps are determining gross pay from hours worked and compensation rate, subtracting pre-tax deductions to establish taxable wages, calculating and withholding federal, state, and local taxes, and subtracting post-tax deductions to reach net pay. The five procedures above expand each of those steps into a named, executable process with prerequisites and expected outcomes, for growth-stage teams running payroll manually or checking what their software already produced.
